skills.when_to_use: Use only when the question explicitly supplies a labeled list of candidate answers and asks to select an answer from that list, with alternatives distinguishable by visible facts or relations across the videos. Acquire neutral evidence for the differences between those answer alternatives. A list of input videos, source-video labels, object markers, or a comparison between two videos does not constitute an answer-choice list. Do not use for open-ended descriptions, explanations, or comparisons without an explicit candidate-answer list.
skills.strategy: For supplied alternatives, identify which visible fact or relation separates the still plausible answers, preserving every qualifier and combination of entities in the question rather than treating an option label as evidence. Use analyze_videos for an independently observable local distinction, passing its exact neutral criterion and necessary context in each videoagent_request instruction without asking the local agent to select an answer option. When the decisive distinction is a cross-video visual relationship, use watch_videos with the relevant relation in instruction, at least two distinct video_id values, and one valid source-second clip per video, without an fps field; locate unknown moments through local requests before choosing narrow clips. Compare each returned fact with the alternatives it actually distinguishes, keeping unsupported, contradicted, and unresolved claims separate; a missing description must not eliminate an alternative by itself. If multiple alternatives remain possible, target the unresolved distinction most likely to change the answer with a neutral follow-up, and reconsider the question's exact conditions when reports support several supposedly exclusive alternatives. Stop when supported distinctions determine the requested answer, or follow the runtime's bounded finalization using the strongest available support and a concise limitation in reason, while preserving the required answer format.
